section-navy6.text: They change what you eat, how you speak, and the shape of your jaw. Teeth shift into the gap, dentures need adhesive to stay put, and missing roots let the jawbone recede. Implants fuse to the bone and stop that drift.

faq.q: How long do dental implants last?
faq.a: With proper care, dental implants are designed to last a lifetime. The titanium post typically never needs replacing. The ceramic crown may need replacement after 15 to 20 years with normal wear. Regular cleanings and checkups are essential for long-term implant health.

faq.q: Does getting a dental implant hurt?
faq.a: Implant placement is performed under local anesthesia or sedation, so you feel no pain during the procedure. Most patients experience mild soreness and swelling for 3 to 5 days afterward, which is managed with over-the-counter pain relievers. Many patients report the procedure was far more comfortable than they expected.

faq.q: Does insurance cover dental implants in Arvada, Colorado?
faq.a: Many dental insurance plans contribute toward the crown portion of an implant. Some plans also cover the surgical placement. We verify your benefits before treatment and help you maximize your coverage. Flexible financing is available to cover any remaining out-of-pocket costs.

faq.q: How long does the dental implant process take?
faq.a: The full implant process typically takes 4 to 8 months from placement to final crown. This includes the 3 to 6 month osseointegration period. For qualifying patients, we offer same-day implants with immediate temporary restorations so you leave with teeth the same day.

faq.q: Am I too old for dental implants?
faq.a: There is no upper age limit for dental implants. Implants are placed in healthy patients well into their 80s. The key factors are adequate bone density, good general health, and absence of uncontrolled systemic conditions. We will evaluate your candidacy at your consultation.

faq.q: What happens if I do not replace a missing tooth?
faq.a: When a tooth is lost, the jawbone at that site begins to deteriorate from lack of stimulation. Surrounding teeth gradually shift toward the gap, affecting your bite and increasing your risk of further tooth loss. Dental implants are the only replacement option that prevents bone loss.

Implant failure is uncommon with a success rate above 95%. Risk factors include smoking, uncontrolled diabetes, and poor oral hygiene. We thoroughly evaluate your health before placement and provide detailed aftercare instructions to maximize your chances of long-term success.
